name: Relic Passive
description: Run-scoped modifiers that fire off events instead of clicks. A relic is a listener with a rule: when combat.entityDefeated fires, heal two; when combat.turnStarted fires, gain one energy. This component owns the roster of held relics, their trigger conditions, and their stacking policy, and it registers every modification through utility.command_bus rather than editing combat math directly — relics that reach inside combat.damage_resolver are how balance dies. It does not own acquisition: relics arrive from shops, drafts, or boss rewards, all of which simply grant an id. And it does not own persistence: a relic is born and dies with the run, so progression.run_meta_progression never hears about it — that separation is the entire difference between a run and an account.

inputs.name: stackingPolicy
inputs.description: unique: duplicates are re-rolled or converted; stack: duplicates multiply the effect; refresh: duplicates renew duration-style relics. unique is the default because it is the only policy that stays auditable at a glance.

inputs.name: maxRelics
inputs.description: Cap on simultaneously held relics. 0 means unlimited — the genre norm, since relic synergy is the fun. Set a cap only if relic count is itself a balance lever.

outputs.name: activeRelics
outputs.description: Relic ids currently held this run, in acquisition order.

outputs.name: relicTriggerCount
outputs.description: Lifetime triggers this run. A relic that never fires is either broken or mis-signed; this count is how you tell.
